'''''Trachelospermum jasminoides''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Apocynaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to eastern and southeastern Asia ([[Japan]], [[Korea]], southern [[China]] and [[Vietnam]]).<ref name=foc>{{cite journal|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200018484|journal=[[Flora of China (series)|Flora of China]]|title=3. Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindley) Lemaire, Jard. Fleur. 1: t. 61. 1851.|volume=16|page=167|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref> [[Common name]]s include '''Confederate jasmine''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TRJA|taxon=Trachelospermum jasminoides|accessdate=12 December 2015}}</ref> '''star jasmine''', '''Confederate jessamine''', and '''Chinese star jessamine'''.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref>

This plant,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/18287/trachelospermum-jasminoides/details|work=[[Royal Horticultural Society]]|title=Trachelospermum jasminoides {{!}} star jasmine|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref> and the [[variegation|variegated]] [[cultivar]] 'Variegatum',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/93768/trachelospermum-jasminoides-variegatum-(v)/details|work=Royal Horticultural Society|title=Trachelospermum jasminoides 'Variegatum' (v) {{!}} variegated Confederate jasmine|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf|work=Royal Horticultural Society|title=AGM Plants - Ornamental|page=103|date=July 2017|access-date=23 December 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
''Trachelospermum jasminoides'' is an [[evergreen]] [[woody plant|woody]] [[liana]] growing to {{convert|10|ft|m|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} high. When they meet a wet surface, they emit aerial weed roots, otherwise they surround the support (they are twining). If cut, like most [[Apocynaceae]], they exude a white [[latex]], resembling sticky milk. Young twigs, initially pubescent, become glabrous with age. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, oval to lanceolate, {{convert|2|-|10|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long and {{convert|1|-|4.5|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} broad, with an entire margin and an acuminate apex. Dark green in summer, the leaves turn bronze in winter.

The fragrant [[flower]]s, which are borne in spring to early summer, are white, {{convert|1|-|2|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} diameter, with a tube-like [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]] opening out into five petal-like lobes. The white, rotate [[actinomorphic]] flowers have a [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] formed by five narrow, smooth, reflexed [[sepal]]s 2−5 mm, much shorter than the corolla tube. The latter has a dilated tube in the middle, 5−10 mm long, terminating in 5 obliquely bypassed lobes, all curved, resembling a helix turning counterclockwise. The five [[stamen]]s are inserted in the middle of the corolla tube.

==Cultivation==
''Trachelospermum jasminoides'' is commonly grown as an [[ornamental plant]] and [[houseplant]]. In gardens, public landscapes, and parks it is used as a climbing [[vine]], a [[groundcover]], and a fragrant potted plant on terraces and patios. It will flower in full sun, partial shade, or total shade, and requires well-drained soil (if constantly kept damp it may succumb to fungal infection), moderate water, moderate fertilizer, and a climbing structure (whether a trellis or another plant is secondary). Propagation is most commonly done with cuttings/clones.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Howard Garrett's Plants for Texas|first=Howard|last=Garrett|page=157|publisher=[[University of Texas Press]]|date=1 June 1996|isbn=978-0292727885}}</ref>

It is widely planted in [[California]] and also particularly in the [[Southeastern United States]], where its hardiness is confined to [[USDA Zone]]s 8–10.

===Nomenclature===
Dictionaries (such as [[Merriam-Webster]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/confederate%20jasmine|work=Merriam Webster|title=confederate jasmine {{!}} noun|access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref> and dictionary.com) suggest that the name '''confederate jasmine''' comes from the plant's common cultivation in the southern United States.

It gets another of its common names, '''trader's compass''', from an old [[Uzbekistan]] saying that it pointed traders in the right direction, provided they were of good character. It is also called '''star jasmine''' in [[Europe]] and '''Chinese jasmine''' or '''Chinese ivy''' in [[Asia]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2023}}

==Uses==
A valuable perfume oil is extracted from the steam distilled or tinctured flowers and used in high end perfumery. 
In a dilute form, tinctured flowers are much used in Chinese, Vietnamese and Thai incenses. A [[bast fibre]] is produced from the stems.<ref name=foc/>

==Chemical constituents==
Five indole alkaloids; [[coronaridine]], [[voacangine]], [[apparicine]], conoflorine, and 19-epi-voacangarine have been reported.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=[[Planta Medica]]|title=Indole Alkaloids from Trachelospermum jasminoides|first1=Talat|last1=Fatima|first2=S|last2=Ijaz|first3=George|last3=Crank|first4=Shaheen|last4=Wasti|date=February 1987|edition=53|volume=1|issue=1 |pages=57–59|doi=10.1055/s-2006-962620|pmid=17268963}}</ref>
